summary: Placer County lookout site on Mosquito Ridge in the Tahoe National Forest; a 1937 newspaper item names a CCC enrollee assigned to it; listed as tower, gone.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as Tower, status Gone; Peakbagging marks it a LO site (building removed or status unknown)

events.note: June 1937 item announces that Henry G. Bucknell, a Civilian Conservation Corps enrollee from Camp Bradley, will be assigned to the Mosquito Ridge lookout under District Ranger Charles Beardsley, Foresthill District; the item announces the assignment and does not confirm service

evidence.supports: site is in the Tahoe National Forest
CCC camp enrollees were appointed to the Tahoe short-term protective force
Henry G. Bucknell is an enrollee in Camp Bradley
the enrollee is named Henry G. Bucknell
evidence.quote: Henry G. Bucknell, enrollee in Camp Bradley

evidence.supports: Bucknell to be assigned to the Mosquito Ridge lookout under District Ranger Charles Beardsley, Foresthill District

evidence.supports: the item is from the Nevada State Journal
Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Mosquito Ridge as a tower, status Gone

evidence.supports: Peakbagging lists Mosquito Ridge as a LO site

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one 1937 newspaper item plus FFLOS and Peakbagging listings. No build date, description, photo or post-1937 account found. The 1937 item announces an assignment, so staffed as_of 1937 is an assignment, not confirmed service. Mapcarta gives 3,510 ft and Peakbagging 3509 ft elevation (not used). The 2022 Mosquito Fire (Placer and El Dorado counties) is a separate topic; no source ties it to this lookout, so it is left out. Natural Atlas calls it a lookout tower, but its page text did not load, so it is not used. Today's condition and access are not described by any source read.
